_note: Concept-demo scenario definitions (2026-08-26 Concept Demo First directive S1/S4). Each scenario declares the node_ids it depends on for its answer -- used by run_corroboration.py to compute the scenario_pass_rate demo-gate metric. These are scenario SHAPES for the demo skill, not frozen golden-set items (no ground-truth answer key here -- that's the eviction-line/Direction-E pattern, out of scope for this milestone per the directive's 'demo harness = the skill itself' framing).

scenarios.title: TX collection-suit answer/SOL scenario
scenarios.description: Person served with a Texas debt-collection lawsuit in justice court; needs to know whether the debt is time-barred and what their answer deadline is.

scenarios.title: CA scenario -- collection-suit SOL/answer
scenarios.description: Person served with a California debt-collection lawsuit; needs SOL posture and answer deadline.

scenarios.title: Pre-suit FDCPA validation-notice / dispute-rights scenario
scenarios.description: Person getting pre-suit collector calls/letters, no lawsuit yet; needs to know their debt-validation and dispute rights under FDCPA S1692g.

scenarios.title: Wage-garnishment scenario (TX + CA)
scenarios.description: Person facing or already subject to wage garnishment on a consumer debt; needs to know what's protected in their state. Deliberately spans both demo states since TX (near-total prohibition) and CA (formula-based limit) illustrate materially different outcomes from the same underlying question.

scenarios.title: Band 3 boundary-marker scenario -- default judgment set-aside
scenarios.description: Person already has a default judgment against them and asks whether it can be undone. Deliberately hits a genuinely discretionary judicial determination (Craddock factors) so the demo shows the system correctly refusing to predict an outcome, naming the deterministic 30-day filing deadline, and pointing to attorney review for the discretionary merits.
